faq.question: How long do I have?
faq.answer: Enrolment for this year closes on the date shown above, and your access lasts a year from the day you start.

faq.question: What do I need to pass?
faq.answer: Every lesson read and every check passed. The final assessment draws 4 questions from a bank of 6, with a 10-minute limit; you can retake it.

faq.question: How long is the certificate valid?
faq.answer: 12 months. It shows its expiry date, and a QR code that opens its verification page.

modules.name: Module 1 · What counts as personal data
modules.description: The data you handle every day, and the kinds that need more care.

pages.title: Welcome, and how this refresher works

fields.objectives: Know what you need to complete; Know how long the certificate lasts

pages.markdown:
This is the yearly refresher. Read each lesson in order — the next opens when you finish the one before — answer the short checks, and finish with the assessment.

**What you need to complete:** every lesson, every check passed, and the final assessment.

**Your certificate** is valid for twelve months. We will remind you before it expires.

pages.title: Personal data, in plain words

fields.objectives: Spot personal data in a spreadsheet, an email and a log file

pages.markdown:
## Anything that identifies a person

A name, an email address, a customer number, an IP address in a server log, a photo from a team event — all personal data, because each one points at a person.

## Special categories

Health, beliefs, union membership, biometric data. These need an explicit reason to process and a smaller audience.

> **Rule of thumb:** if you would mind it being forwarded to the whole company, it needs care.

pages.title: Where it lives in our tools

fields.objectives: List the three places personal data piles up unnoticed

pages.markdown: Shared drives, chat threads and exported CSVs. Each is a copy nobody tracks. Before you export, ask whether a link to the system that already holds it would do.

pages.title: Last year’s version of this module
pages.markdown: Kept for the record. The current module replaces it.

modules.name: Module 2 · Sharing and incidents
modules.description: The three questions before you share, and the hour after something goes wrong.

pages.title: Three questions before you share

fields.objectives: Ask: who needs it, what is the least they need, how will it travel

pages.markdown:
1. **Who needs it?** A person with a reason, not a channel.
2. **What is the least they need?** A count instead of a list, a list without the email column.
3. **How will it travel?** Through the system, not an attachment.

pages.title: The first hour of an incident

fields.objectives: Report within the hour; Keep the evidence

pages.markdown:
Sent the file to the wrong person? Lost a laptop? **Report it within the hour** through the incident form — not by fixing it quietly. The clock for telling the regulator starts when we know, so the earlier the better.

Keep the evidence: do not delete the email you sent by mistake.

pages.markdown: The full data-protection policy lives in the handbook.

questions.prompt: An IP address in a server log can be personal data.
questions.explanation: It can point at a person, so it counts.

questions.prompt: Which of these are special categories?
questions.explanation: Health and union membership need an explicit reason to process.

questions.prompt: Within how many hours should you report an incident? (a number)
A colleague asks for the customer list to “check something”. What do you send first?
choices: A question: what do you need it for?

questions.prompt: Deleting the wrongly-sent email is the right first step.
Which travels personal data most safely?
choices: A link into the system that holds it
